blocks.text: NEW YORK, United States — New York postponed the iconic Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday over fears of extreme weather, a first in the event’s 100-year history, as a major storm gathers steam on the US East Coast. The brewing “nor’easter” threatens to disrupt plans for millions of people hitting the road and flying around the Thursday holiday, one of the country’s busiest travel seasons. “With severe weather expected on Thanksgiving Day, and out of an abundance of caution, in partnership with the City the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed,” Macy’s told AFP in a statement.
